s.note: Crisp radishes on salted butter and biscuits.
s.how: Rub the cold butter into the flour with a pinch of salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Pat out 3cm thick, cut rounds and bake at 220C until risen and golden. Slice the radishes thinly. Split the warm biscuits, spread thickly with soft butter and pile on radishes, salt flakes and chives.

s.note: Golden yolks whipped with mustard and paprika. $150 in gold for one dance.
s.how: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for 10 minutes, then cool in iced water. Peel, halve and mash the yolks with the mayo, mustard, vinegar and salt. Pipe or spoon back into the whites. Dust with paprika and scatter with chives.

m.note: Slow-roast pork shoulder with vinegar slaw.
m.how: Rub the pork with the sugar, paprika, garlic powder and plenty of salt. Roast covered at 160C until it pulls apart easily. Warm 100ml of the vinegar with the chilli flakes and a pinch of sugar for a sauce. Toss the cabbage and carrot with the rest of the vinegar and salt. Pull the pork, splash with the chilli vinegar and serve with the slaw and rolls.

m.note: Lamb racks under a bright green herb crust. Scarlett's dress from the green drapes.
m.how: Blitz the parsley, mint, garlic, breadcrumbs and 2 tbsp oil to a bright green crumb. Sear the lamb racks all over in the rest of the oil, then brush with mustard and press on the crumb. Roast at 200C until pink in the middle, then rest. Boil the potatoes, toss with butter and serve with the carved cutlets.

w.note: Baked peaches under a buttermilk crust with cream.
w.how: Toss the peaches with the brown sugar, cornflour and cinnamon in a baking dish. Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and bake at 190C until golden and bubbling. Serve warm with the cream.

d.note: Bourbon over crushed ice with fresh mint.
d.how: Heat the sugar and water until dissolved, add half the mint and cool. Pack 4 cups with crushed ice, add 60ml bourbon and a splash of strained syrup to each. Stir until frosted and crown with mint.
